A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCG front-door identification research. Their text, equations and diagrams are readable, including v2's complete Appendix A. v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical definitions, lemmas, proofs and illustrative causal graphs, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, including Appendix A. Its sedation and blood-pressure example is explicitly conceptual and reports no patient data or measured outcomes.

M1.justification: The identification procedure changes substantially. Compared with v1's Definition 6, v2's Definition 7 adds the self-loop case without confounding between X and its ancestors. Theorem 1 revises the adjustment sets and identification formula, including case-dependent conditioning on later instances of X. These changes affect applicability and computation, rather than merely renaming the criterion.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or performs empirical tasks. The added clinical scenario and expanded causal-graph examples illustrate theoretical applicability rather than introduce evaluated data coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimental baseline comparisons. v2 adds an analytical comparison with the Granger front-door criterion, but this concerns theoretical soundness and research positioning rather than an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol, data splits, performance metrics or training budgets. Changes to graph assumptions and illustrative temporal lags concern the mathematical analysis.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness studies or error analyses appear in either version. v2's additional counterexamples and conceptual clinical application are theoretical and explanatory, without a data-backed case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's positivity restriction is an identifiability assumption, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither PDF reports numerical evaluation results or empirical qualitative findings. The added and revised identification results are mathematical contributions, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's temporal-independence assumption for latent variables, explicitly formalizes temporal priority, permits bidirected SCG self-loops, and changes the positivity requirements. It revises the conditioning-set lemmas and Theorem 1, and adds the self-loop Lemma 4.3. Appendix A contains new Properties 1–2 and revised proofs alongside relocated material. Section 3 also develops counterexamples to naive front-door identification.

C1.justification: The overall identification objective remains, but v2 substantially revises its contribution claims. Its introduction explicitly claims first nonparametric graphical identification in the stated setting, including within-series latent confounding, and presents the unsuitability of standard and Granger front-door criteria as a contribution. Its conclusion narrows the guarantee from any underlying distribution to positive distributions.

C2.justification: New Section 3 explains how temporal aggregation hides back-door paths and why cycles can make adjustment invalid. Expanded discussion distinguishes identification from estimation and single-series observations from repeated observations. v2 also explains the strict-positivity limitation and adds a conceptual clinical application. The earlier limitation that the criterion is sufficient but incomplete remains.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies software implementation details, hardware, computational budgets, hyperparameters or code/data access instructions. The additional technical material consists of mathematical definitions and derivations.

R1.justification: v1 broadly states that prior work did not address identification beyond adjustment under hidden confounding. v2 acknowledges earlier time-series front-door results and distinguishes their assumptions, separates micro-effect identification from cluster-level effects, and discusses concurrent frequency-domain work. Additions include Eichler and Didelez (2010), Ferreira and Assaad (2024, 2025), and Reiter et al. (2024); the Forré and Mooij reference is removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and preliminaries, inserts a dedicated section explaining the inadequacy of existing criteria, and replaces inline lemma proofs with extended intuition and examples while placing proofs in Appendix A. Terminology, the title and the identification-versus-estimation explanation are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes the opening illustrations into a nine-panel Figure 1, expands the identifying graph examples across Figures 2–3, and adds Figure 5's four detailed conditioning-set diagrams. The non-identifiability examples are retained and redrawn. Mediators and adjustment sets receive additional color coding, captions expand, and typography and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves accessibility and precision through its explanation of front-door failures, clearer positioning against prior time-series work, and explicit positivity qualification. The revised proofs and graphical explanations make the reasoning easier to inspect. However, the new worked formula on page 15 omits the marginal weighting required by Equation 1 and writes an observational rather than interventional target. These material inconsistencies limit the net quality improvement despite the substantial revision.
